title: trifolium alexandrinum subsp. berytheum
intro: Trifolium alexandrinum subsp. berytheum, commonly known as Syrian clover, is a subspecies of clover native to the Mediterranean region. It is used in traditional medicine due to its health benefits, which include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Syrian clover include wound healing, pain relief, and the treatment of gastrointestinal disorders, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins. The bioactive compounds present in Syrian clover also exhibit potential in the prevention of various diseases, including cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disorders.
